name: Deficit Barbell Bent-Over Row
description: The deficit barbell row is performed with the lifter standing on elevated plates or a platform, allowing the barbell to descend lower than floor level. This increased range of motion provides a greater lat stretch at the bottom of each repetition and may enhance muscle fiber recruitment through the extended pull. The exercise requires superior hamstring flexibility and hip hinge mechanics compared to a standard barbell row.

execution.starting_position: Stand on 2-4 bumper plates or a low platform (2-4 inches elevation). Position the barbell over the mid-foot. Hinge at the hips to approximately parallel with the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Stack plates or use a wooden platform. Ensure the surface is stable and will not shift. The deficit increases the bottom ROM of each rep.
steps: Step 1: Stand on the elevated platform with the barbell hanging below the platform level.
Step 2: Hinge at the hips until the torso is near parallel, maintaining a neutral spine.
Step 3: Brace the core, retract the scapulae, and pull the bar toward the lower sternum.
Step 4: Squeeze rhomboids and lats at the top of the movement.
Step 5: Lower the bar past the platform edge under full control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before each rep. Exhale through the pull.
common_mistakes: Using a platform so high that lumbar rounding occurs to reach the bar
Not controlling the eccentric, letting the bar drop past the platform level
Insufficient hamstring flexibility causing the hips to rise
safety_considerations: Requires good hamstring flexibility — do not force depth beyond what neutral spine allows
Use a stable, non-slip platform only
Reduce weight relative to your standard barbell row
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Bar descends below platform level at the bottom, pulled to lower sternum at the top.
coaching_cues: Let the bar drop below the platform
Spine stays neutral even at the extended bottom position
Pull with the elbows, not the hands
